paragraphs.text: Self-evolving pitfall immunity for coding agents: a failed-then-fixed tool call becomes a rule, inje
cted before the mistake repeats. Try: npx dsh-immune-system demo
Your coding agents stop re-debugging what they already fixed.
English | 简体中文
When a tool call fails and the next attempt fixes it, the plugin saves that pair as a rule. Rules th
at match the current work get injected into context on later runs, before the agent repeats the same
the current work get injected into context on later runs, before the agent repeats the same mistake.
One `core/` engine, two hosts, one npm package: **DSH** (DeepSeek Harness, checked against the real
host contract) and **ZCode** (checked against its hook lifecycle).
### Quick demo
Runs the whole pipeline in memory, installs nothing, writes nothing:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
It distills a failure→success episode, recalls it from a paraphrased prompt, and prints the `<immune
_memory>` block the hooks inject.
### Install
**DSH** — from npm (prebuilt, no toolchain):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Same package from a tarball or from git:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The `github:` form builds at install time through `prepare`, which pnpm blocks until it is allowlist
ed (the Chinese README has the exact setting). npm or the tarball sidesteps that.
Restart DSH afterwards; plugin bundles are composed at startup.
**ZCode** — this repository is itself a marketplace source:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Start a new task afterwards; existing tasks keep the capability catalog they started with.
### After installing: what you should see
Run the self-check first; it is the same command support will ask you for:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Eight checks: Node ≥ 22.5, an FTS5 trigram probe (plus the two-character-CJK fallback), both databas
es readable, the marker file, the MCP script, the native-UI contract, and the counters. Non-zero exi
t means the next session will be missing something.
Then, plainly, what is proven and what is not:
* **Hooks** — verified against the real DSH event bus and the real ZCode hook lifecycle (`scripts/ve

rify-live-host.mjs`, `scripts/verify-client-serve.mjs`).
* **The ZCode settings tab** — mounted and
serving `/plugins/<id>/client.js`; it has not been driven end-to-end in a browser here. If it does n

ot appear, the data is still reachable through `immune list` and `immune ui`.
* **External LLM disti
llation** — works against one real OpenAI-compatible endpoint (SenseNova). Other providers share the
code path but are untested. Without `IMMUNE_LLM_BASE_URL` and `IMMUNE_LLM_MODEL` the deterministic
rule path runs and the model counters stay at zero. `node scripts/verify-llm.mjs` is the one-command

check when you have an endpoint.
* **`IMMUNE_GUARD=warn` is ZCode-only.** On DSH a configured guard
still **denies**: the host contract offers allow/deny/ask with no advisory mode. Keep `IMMUNE_GUARD
=off` (the default) if you do not want denial.
### Sharing what it learned
[代码示例省略，未执行]
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The dashboard's `/api/export?format=json` produces a snapshot that `immune import` reads back, so a
team can start from one person's proven rules.
### Syncing into AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md
Agents that do not run these hooks still read the project docs, so learned rules can be exported int
that do not run these hooks still read the project docs, so learned rules can be exported into them:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Rules land between `` markers. Everything outside them is left alone, angle brackets inside rules ar
e stripped, and re-running rewrites the block instead of appending.
To do that automatically after each turn's distillation:

* `IMMUNE_SYNC_DOC=AGENTS.md` (or `1` for the default target)
* `IMMUNE_SYNC_DOC_MIN_HITS=3` (rules
below this hit count are not exported)
### Benchmarks and CI
Every push runs the retrieval gate and unit suite on Node 22 and 24:
* **Test suite** — `npm test` runs **138 tests**, 0 failures. `scripts/verify-*.mjs` add 15 + 24 + 2
0 host-level assertions, and `verify-installed.mjs` adds 22 against your installed profile. Those ar

e the numbers you can reproduce locally.
* **Recall** — fixed zh/en matrix with 8 paraphrased positi
ves and 6 gram-clean negatives. Current: R@1 100%, R@3 100%, FP 0%. CI fails below R@3 7/8 or above

FP 1/6.
* **Index and query speed** (`scripts/bench-scale.mjs`) — 300 rules index in 41 ms (0.14 ms/

rule); 67 matches run at p50 0.38 ms, p95 0.75 ms.
* **Hook latency** (`scripts/bench-tool-latency.m

js`) — the tool path never calls a model; distillation is paid at the turn boundary.
* **Live LLM ch
eck** (`scripts/verify-llm.mjs`) — one command against a configured endpoint, when there is one.
### Comparison
|  | dsh-plugin-immune | deja-vu | mem0 | claude-memory-compiler |
| Keeps | failure→success pairs distilled into rules | full session transcripts | conversation facts

| compiled skill files |
| Delivery | injected before the repeat, via hooks | search on demand (MCP

/TUI) | SDK-level recall | skill file, read by the model |
| Dependencies | none (`node:sqlite` FTS5

) | one Go binary | Python + store | Node |
| Hosts | DSH, ZCode | Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, 36+ |
any via SDK | Claude Code |
Different jobs, mostly: deja-vu indexes everything you did and searches it; this keeps the lessons a
nd pushes them in unasked.
### Design notes
**Outcome detection.** A non-zero exit is not an error result on either host: ZCode only fires `Post
ToolUseFailure` when a handler throws, and DSH reports non-zero exits rather than flagging them. Bot
h adapters therefore classify the result themselves, in this order: structured `value.exitCode`; `is
Error` or an `error` payload; a trailing `[exit code: N]` / `[killed by signal: X]` / timeout marker
; and a narrow marker regex. A structured payload with no exit status counts as success and its text
is not scanned, so reading a log that mentions `Error:` stays a success.
